import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load data from csv file
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Convert date to datetime object for easier plotting
coffee_sales['date'] = coffee_sales['date'].dt.date

# Create bar chart to visualize sales by product
product_sales = coffee_sales.groupby('product')['total'].sum().reset_index()
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(data=product_sales, x='product', y='total', ci=None)
plt.title('Total Sales by Product')
plt.xlabel('Product')
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create pie chart to visualize payment method distribution
payment_method_dist = coffee_sales['payment_method'].value_counts().reset_index()
payment_method_dist.columns = ['payment_method', 'frequency']
plt.figure(figsize=(8,8))
sns.set_palette('viridis')
plt.pie(payment_method_dist['frequency'], labels=payment_method_dist['payment_method'], autopct='%1.1f%%')
plt.title('Payment Method Distribution')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('payment_method_dist.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create scatter plot to visualize relationship between price and quantity
plt.figure(figsize=(10,8))
sns.scatterplot(data=coffee_sales, x='price', y='quantity')
plt.title('Relationship between Price and Quantity')
plt.xlabel('Price ($)')
plt.ylabel('Quantity')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('price_quantity_scatter.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
